gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much a Creality printer-plus-scanner bundle actually saves compared with buying the same printer and scanner separately from Creality's own store today. The real saving is $169.80 (11.9%) for the K1 Max + Raptor, $239 (10.6%) for the K2 Pro Combo + Raptor Pro and $389 (15.0%) for the K2 Plus + Raptor Pro. Creality's own 'Save' labels claim $1,039.80, $539 and $589.
standout_why: I compared these pages: the cited store.creality.com Scanner Combo collection and the K2 Plus scanner combo page, plus 3dprintmates.com, rottenwifi.com and notebookcheck.net (Sermoon P1 with a free SPARKX i7). The Creality pages show only struck-through compare-at prices and 'Save $X' figures measured against those prices. The K2 Plus combo page contradicts itself: $1,799 now, $2,699 compare-at, but 'Save $809'. 3dprintmates lists scanners only, with no printers or bundles. Rottenwifi lists separate sale and regular prices and loose 'planning bands' such as '$1,500–$2,500 combined', and it computes no bundle saving. Notebookcheck gives the free printer's $399 retail price but no combined saving. None of them adds up the separate prices today against the bundle price.
decides: A Creality bundle saves the shopper about $170–$390, or 11–15%. That is a real discount, but it is a third to a sixth of what the store's labels suggest. Buying the printer and scanner separately costs only 11–15% more, and it lets the shopper mix brands, such as a scanner Dealectric lists (3DMakerpro, Revopoint) with a QIDI or Flashforge printer. So the pick should be whichever scanner fits the objects being scanned, not 'buy the bundle'. Of the bundles, the K2 Plus + Raptor Pro saves the most in both dollars and percent ($389, 15%). Its page doesn't confirm whether the CFS unit is included (see unsourced). The ChatGPT card 'Otter Lite+3D Printer All-In-One Combo' can't be checked, because its page doesn't name the printer.
